primary_meaning: Believers/disciples who must remain united to Christ (the true vine) in order to live and bear fruit; unfruitful branches are pruned or cast away

alternatives.meaning: The covenant people of God (natural Israel as original olive branches; Gentile believers as wild branches grafted in)
Tokens of victory, triumph, festal joy or praise (especially palm branches)
Messianic scion or royal Davidic line (usually the singular 'Branch')

notes: The term is strongly context-dependent; no single fixed symbol covers every biblical occurrence. The vine-and-branches metaphor of John 15 is by far the most frequently invoked in Christian teaching and devotion for personal union with Christ, while the olive-tree image of Romans 11 is equally standard for ecclesiological and salvation-historical discussion. Palm-branch imagery forms a separate, well-attested festive/victory motif.
